summary.headline: LatentView Q4 FY26: dollar revenue up ~17% YoY, FY26 crossed INR1,000 crore; FY27 visibility guided at 12-13% organic, with 18-20% target.
summary.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue crossing INR1,000 crore, with dollar growth of about 20% for the year (organic ~18.2-18.3% excluding one quarter of Decision Point). Q4 dollar revenue rose about 17% YoY (about 24.3% in rupee terms) and was up about 0.5% QoQ despite a large technology-account shrinkage. Adjusted EBITDA was about 24.1% in Q4 with a 1.1% forex benefit, offset by travel, visa and hiring costs; full-year business EBITDA was 23%. Management guided FY27 EBITDA to 21-22% at a planning rate of INR92/USD, citing upfront AI CoE and Databricks leadership hiring.

segments.name: Technology
segments.commentary: Top technology account shrinkage totalled about $6.5-7 million versus the $5.5-6 million earlier estimated; management expects to recoup 50-60% of lost annual contract value and guides FY27 technology growth at 5-8% YoY.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Revenue of about $18 million in FY26 after growth over 80%; management guides FY27 growth of at least about 40%, with new logos signed in wealth/asset management and payments.

segments.name: CPG and retail
segments.commentary: Strength in Q4 driven partly by Decision Point (acquired) and a one-off large consumer project that will taper in Q1 FY27; FY27 growth guided at 18-22%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic dollar growth visibility of 12-13% from current order book and high-probability pipeline; management targets 18-20%, typically adding 8-10 percentage points through the year.
FY27 EBITDA guided at 21-22%, based on INR92/USD planning rate; current rates of INR95-96 may provide currency benefit, not factored in.
Technology vertical FY27 growth 5-8% YoY; BFSI at least about 40%; CPG and retail 18-22%.
Databricks portfolio expected to keep growing about 60%+ in FY27.
Gross margin levers from nearshore/offshore shift and AI projects at 55-58% gross margin; not factored into planning.
Plan to raise share of fixed-bid/outcome-linked contracts above the current 18-20%.
capex_capacity: Utilisation rose to about 89% in Q4 from about 85%, driven by a one-off consumer project spanning Q4 to June.
Continued investment in senior AI CoE and Databricks leadership hiring, including a potential CTO hire; GTM investment largely complete per management, with possible Europe hires.
Evaluating inorganic acquisitions with strong Databricks professional services partnerships.
Claude certification program: over 200 enrolled, about 40 in final stage.
demand_pricing: About 28% of FY25 revenue involved AI where visible to clients (generative/agentic); a further 21% had AI under the hood, so about half of work has some AI component.
AI-led projects earn gross margins of about 55-58% versus company-wide 50.8%.
Deal sizes range from about $0.25 million to $2-3 million; three large deals in the top technology account were discussed, one of them $3 million-plus and near closing.
Management says clients are paying similar or slightly higher budgets for more output; no rate deflation seen on T&M work.
Pricing mix: about 80% T&M (of which 65-68% is managed services, capacity-based) and about 20% fixed-bid; no material outcome-based pricing today.
Partnerships: Anthropic discussed as a services partner (not a client); Databricks professional services partnership being deepened.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the sequential drop in technology larger than guided in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Shrinkage in the top technology account was about $6.5-7 million versus the $5.5-6 million guided; management says all renewals and rationalisation are now complete and expects to recoup 50-60% of lost value.

qa_highlights.question: Is the flat QoQ BFSI growth in Q4 due to a one-off in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BFSI share rose from 14% to about 16% QoQ and BFSI ended FY26 near $18 million; incremental growth rates will slow from a higher base.

qa_highlights.question: What is the organic FY26 growth and FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic FY26 growth was about 18.2-18.3%; FY27 visibility is 12-13% with an 18-20% target; guidance is in USD, not constant currency.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margins miss the expected 24.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Professional and consultant charges for senior AI CoE and Databricks hires weighed on EBITDA; adjusting for them, margin would have been closer to 24.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI revenue treated versus token costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Clients pay for LLM infrastructure and tokens; reported revenue is entirely LatentView's services revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What drives technology vertical decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Vendor consolidation and insourcing by a new leader in the top account; management says budgets have not shrunk and clients are paying similar amounts for more output.

risks_watch: Technology vertical decline in the top account (about $6.5-7 million lost); recovery of 50-60% of lost value depends on deals closing in the next one to two quarters.
DSO rising to about 80 days in FY26 with CPG (90-120 day terms) mix; collections after year-end to be tracked.
Margin pressure from senior AI and Databricks hiring in FY27; FY27 EBITDA guided lower at 21-22%.
CPG one-off project tapering in Q1 FY27, which will pressure utilisation and CPG growth.
Shift from managed services and T&M to outcome-based pricing unproven; management will report results quarterly.
Competitive risk from OpenAI and Anthropic building services arms; management says it is too early to see impact.
summary.management_tone: Confident on AI traction, Databricks and BFSI, but cautious on technology vertical visibility and FY27 organic growth (12-13% visibility versus 18-20% target). Management was candid on Q4 margin shortfall and the need for upfront hiring investment.
key_quotes: So, in general, I feel more optimistic. I mean the percentages and stuff we will obviously see as things pan out over the next one, two quarters.
There has not been any shrinkage of budgets itself that we have seen.
The Databricks portfolio of work will continue to grow at about 60% plus.
So that 20% that Raj referred to, we want to bump it up, okay.

growth.why: FY27 organic dollar growth visibility guided at 12-13% from order book and high-probability pipeline (target 18-20%), with EBITDA 21-22% at INR92/USD; no capacity additions, backing is order book and pipeline without specific contract numbers beyond a few large deals.
